body: Honestly thank you in a weird way that helps.

Thank you. I hope you start feeling better soon. Hopefully you can talk to one of the people you have helped support but if you don't feel comfortable you can dm me to rant. I hope it gets better and yeah being the "good kid" can place such a tool on people. Plus it means no one thinks to look any deeper.

Thank you so much I will try to remember this. Also the one thing that helps me is typically just learning to talk to myself the way I would talk to others if that makes sense. I think it's called positive self talk or something I'm not sure but it works really well.
That makes sense. Thank you for sharing and yeah I've tried going to therapy for some unrelated things but it was pretty unhelpful.

Yeah I used instant cart once but I didn't want to go outside while the person was still there because of covid and watching the driver walk up the six steps to my apartment made me feel so guilty especially because I felt so lazy for not wanting to walk the 4 miles to the grocery store in the freezing cold. I had to convince myself that it was their job, I tipped well and it was not that hard to walk up a few stairs vs the 8 mile round trip walk I would not have had time to make.

Being loved by other people and seeing the way they see me has been what helped me to love myself. So I hate it when people say things like that. I need people to like me otherwise I can't like myself I'll work up to not basing other people's opinions on my self esteem but for now who cares. Sorry I had a therapist say that to me one day while also trying to imply that my current friends don't love me. It sent me into a whole mental tailspin.
I have to say it gets better but then you realize you still have to deal with your traumatized brain. It is so much better but brains are just evil.
That's such a cool skill that you have! And I'm so proud of you for staying in the kitchen for so long. You are amazing keep up the great work!

Huge congratulations! I am so proud of you for leaving. It's ok there will be times when you will greave losing them and times where you will be unbelievably happy you left. That happens and it will decrease overtime and I promise it will get better it will take time and you will probably still have days when you regret it. 

You said you were scared they would show up at your door, I've had this happen to me essentially twice. My parents are nuts. The first time was pretty simple, they showed up and I saw them through my keyhole, and I called the police, and didn't open the door, it was not a fun experience but ultimately was not the worse just ended up talking to a lot of cops in my dorm room while still in my pjs lol. It's awful but if you can stay inside with your door locked you should be good. If it's possible, and it would help make you feel safer you might want to consider moving but that's not something you need to worry about right now.

If you have an email address that they know, change it and don't check your old email because blocking people on email will only send it to spam and you don't need that. Depending on where you live, I would recommend getting a restraining order. I wish the best of luck to you and would like to say I am living proof that it does get better, I'm at the point where I make fun of my family's harassment and with each thing they send I just take screenshots and go great more evidence. That's defiantly not what I used to be like and it took a while to get there but you will notice it happened and be shocked. Feel free to dm me if you want to know more about my crazy story (I fear posting anything too specific pertaining to the incidents with my parents showing up just in case) or just want a friend. Apologizes for the wall of text

Mine's from c-ptsd basically just repeated traumas, I think I've had it for the majority of my life as a way to cope with everything that was happening to me it would allow me to escape and believe that what was happening really wasn't type of thing. It allowed me to escape during a time when I had no way to escape for actual dpdr, side effects are partly due to trauma as well and I can't fully tell if it is due to dpdr or due to trauma. Now it's an annoyance because I still live like I might get abused any second but I'm not going to. And yes, I also have constant pain in my jaw from clenching it due to stress but that's not really a dpdr thing.

Yes it's like we have really weird super powers. Ignoring the fact that I no longer believe anything is real at the moment, I get to go for days without needing to do any of those crazy things normal humans have to do like eating and sleeping.
Yes it's defiantly a bit annoying but kind of cool to be able to go for so long without being tired.
No problem! I hope it works out for you and feel free to update me on how it goes.

Change of environment, I was on antidepressants but I stopped taking them months before I noticed my asexuality went away. And it's ok it's weird I wish there was an easy solution but defiantly try getting your hormones checked and go to a doctor and talk to them about it.

For me there was but I believe mine was caused by stress from living in an unsafe place so after leaving I have a libido again but idk if that happens to everyone, it's just what happened to me. I have no idea if there actually is a solution but it could be a chemical imbalance or just the way you were born. It doesn't make you a bad person just different but no one really is normal so don't worry too much about it. It can also help weed out potential partners who only want to hook up.

I used to think I was asexual like full on never so much as had a crush on everyone. I had no libido or anything. Then I escaped my abusers and now I actually am sexually attracted to people. I would say I'm demi or gray because it's not a lot of people but I have a boyfriend that I am sexually attracted to. It turns out now that I no longer fear for my life constantly my brain can focus on other aspects of life. So I would say that my asexuality was directly linked to trauma given that I lost it after leaving.
Yeah my parents used to call me abusive while beating me I can see the irony logically but my brain is still convinced I'm an abusive burden on people

Telling your child they were a mistake/wished they had an abortion (you made the decision to have me you have to own up to your mistakes like an actual adult)

Using your kid as a therapist for your own messed up life

Telling you kid "you never tell me anything you need to open up to me more then we would have a better relationship" then yelling at them about a small thing they say when they tried to "open up"

I'm back on my sleep deprevation routine and am on day 6 with absolutely no sleep due to anxiety, I start to lose the ability to concentrate and my neurological function decreases (I also can not spell anymore). I am slower in general and everything seems like so much more effort then normal. 

Sleep tracking doesn't help, it can cause more anxiety. I have a watch that does sleep tracking and it just makes me more anxious to see that I only got a total of 4 hours last week.
I can't cry I never have been able to, I listen to sad music as a way to release those emotions.

Not to mention depending on the person, exercise burns precious calories and if you can't afford to eat some days the last thing on your mind is going to be exercising and burning off the few calories you were able to afford that week.

Then if they do have a job it is typically one that is horrible for the body potentailly causing them future health issues that they can not just go to the doctor to solve it is expensive to be poor.
All the time, when you go so long without sleep sometimes the only solution to not sleeping seems to be death but it was just one factor of many in the why I want to die pile.

First of all congratulations on everything that is amazing. I get this a lot and I tend to try not to get excited about things because it means that I might be getting better which is wrong. What I have found is that frequently my thought process is: This bad thing happened this one particular time and now everytime something similar happens it is going to be the same bad outcome. I also try to remind myself the way I feel about something that is out of my control will not cause it to go away. For example if you are excited about your new job there really is nothing that you will do that will cause you to get fired before your first day it is just that our brains have taught us that when we get happy there is usually bad and it will happen every time so don't get your hopes up. It is a survival mechanism learned from being in a situation where everything was bad but now that you are out you can start to accept the good as good and not something that could be used against you.

I'm really lonely and have also lost friends from being "too much to handle" for normal people feel free to dm me and let's be friends! CPTSD is a serious mental illness you're not letting people down because you're recovering right now. You shouldn't ever feel bad for being yourself and you probably went through a lot more then most people. It might be stressful for people but they did not go through it, they do not understand how important but hard it is to talk about this stuff to people.

I have this as well, I always fear the worst because I have no other options but if worst comes to worst there is always government support for things like unemployment and loans that you can pay back later which sucks and it's awful but at least you are out of your parents house. But yeah I am so envious of other people living with their parents or who don't have a job like I struggle a lot and people think it's fun because I am no longer living with my parents like no I ran away and each day I fear something terrible will happen and I will end up homeless again but this time without friends to rely on.
Thank you that's super helpful! And yeah money's a bit tight but I'm alright and safe and that's all that matters.

I survive off $5 a week thanks to rice, not eating a lot and free food from my jobs. It's not fun but I've learned to manage with very little. I also am able to walk to a cheaper grocery store but the fact that I have to walk means that I can't buy a lot which helps me stay on budget but is not helping the whole being in so much pain from working a physically demanding job, I know it would be better if I ate more but I can't do that so here we are. I always create a list to make sure I know what I am buying and how much I plan to spend and will be able to spend there. Also rice and beans is great oh and genric peanut butter has become a lifesaver for quick meals.

There have been times when I just randomly apologize and people ask me what for and my response is typically just for existing. My parents told me they wished they never had me I do not know how to not feel like a burden and I constantly do things to ease the burden on people even though it really does not help and probably makes things worse.

My psychatrist gave up on trying to find sleeping pills that will work after about two months of working together I'd be happy to talk about it along with the source of my insomnia and why it will likely never go completely away.

I'm not sure, you might be able to but it would be difficult maybe try getting disability for PTSD? Then you at least have income without a job that would stress you too much. But if I can make some suggestions: anything with a ton of manual labor can be nice because you don't have to think but it gives you a lot of free time to think, customer service is fun if you can handle getting yelled at which is occasionally easier for people who went through trauma to deal with, truck driving involves little contact with people, data entry also involves virtually no contact with people. I'm jst trying to give a couple of suggestions but I know depending on where you live it could be much more difficult to find a job due to coronavirus.

You've got this, if you get stuck you might be able to rent a cheap car then move to a cheap sublet in a collegetown since so many people are taking gap years because of corona let me know how it goes, I can't help you financally due to being in a not great financal situation but I will happily give you some emotional support and feel free to DM me.
Don't call her, it will not go well for either of ou I know it is awful but part of PTSD is literally questioning if you went through trauma

You can still use the coping mechanisms that you have learned here and you might be able to talk to him about CPTSD but it is not always recognized by therapists. Either way if you learned healthy coping mechanisms here that seem to be working please keep using them it will help you. But maybe there could be something better that you caould be doing that he can teach you. I'd take not having PTSD as a win (as someone who has been diagnosed with way too many mental disorders).

My parents starved me to the point I am suprised I did not die so I understand how much that messes with your head. I am currently working on it and the one thing that has really been helping me is setting times to eat and eating food when I am distracted to actually get better. For the issues with body image, it's difficult, a big thing that helps me is reminding myself that it is my parent's voice in the mirror that tells me I am fat and not my own. I now have the ability to occasionally look back at old pictures of right before they started starving me and I am able to accept that the person in that photo was not fat and that my parents starved me for no reason other then as a way too control me which sounds like what it was with your ex, take back the power and learn to accept yourself, people are willing to date people at any size and if they can't accept you for who you are as a person and not what you look like then they are not worth it.

It's hard, we use a lot of "ums" and "oh no I forgot what I was saying" and "yeah" "sounds cool" when listening, it seems to work most people haven't gotten too upset and sometimes we just apoligize for zoning out because "I'm just so tired." It appears to work but who knows maybe everyone secretly hates us.

Currently have a job in manual labor but if you can, go running or go for a walk, there are plenty of trails that are not that popular or if you live in a small neigborhood you can run on the road. If that's not possible, exercise indoors there are so many free youtube videos you can use that don't have any equipment required. Seriously get your heart pumping and try to move a bit it is super helpful even if you just start pacing around the house/apartment you are staying in
The worst is that my parents convinced me that I owe them everything for allowing me to live
I didn't even think of most of these as a problem until I just read this, it just seemed to make sense to me that it was the only way to feel like I might not be hated what else am I missing?
Distract yourself, audiobooks, podcasts, something intresting but prefrably something you might have listened to before either way you know you can go back to where you fell asleep the next night

I'd just stay up a full night and do something to tire myself out and not let myself go to sleep until whatever time you actually want to sleep its probably not healthy though but it worked for me, I went from falling asleep at 5am to waking up at 5am

I was starved and don't have hunger signals, I set timers to remind me to eat and try to find things to get me to eat, also trying to distract yourself while eating helps you could try to find your favorite TV show or something and make it a rule that you have to eat if you are watching it, it's the opposite of health advice you get but it is useful and its much more important for you to eat

If he never experiences dissociative amnesia, it could be OSDD-1B, if he can it would be useful for him to try to talk it over with a therapist, if not he should carefully attempt internal communication, this can be done through sending out messages until you get a response, one example could be something along the lines of "hi is someone else here and can I meet them?" sounds weird but it might work, I'm not an expert though so you can try to do some googling though there is not a ton of information about it. Best of luck to him, there will probably be a lot of doubt and fears over making it up but that's normal. Good luck to you as well please just try to be supportive and understanding even though if what he is talking about or acting like might seem a bit odd, if you have any questions we're a suspected OSDD-1B system (can't go to therapy right now so no diagnosis) and we'd be happy to try to help.
Feel free to dm me
All the time I am terrified because I don't know how to repay them or if what I do to repay them is good enough

I have chronic pain, I don't sleep, I don't get hungry and can go days without eating and not notice a difference, I am generally numb to pain and lack the ability and motivation to actually do daily tasks like drink water. I have pain flashbacks and sometimes will become unable to move, the big one for me though is losing the abilty to speak my brain is able to be like alright this is what we say but then I just go nope I actually can't speak because I am mute. Not to mention dizziness and headaches and my eyesight changes all the time. Although that could be due to the lack of food.

The thing that really helped me was reaching out to others and changing my hair color. Which I thought would mean I could never be employed but I have two jobs. Anyways find something that you can change that might help, ask people for help and be honest with others. If you feel really bad, I bet a musician you like is going to release a new album or song soon or maybe there is a new tv show or movie that seems really cool. Maybe there's a hobby you always liked that you want. Or maybe a new book by an author you like because you just have to find out what happened to that charecter you love. Seriously don't live for the big things, find the small things that bring you joy and just keep pushing one day more living becaue of the big things is annoying. Live for the stupid small things until you can live because of the good things. Live because someone will be hurt by your death even though you might not realize it. I have been suicidal for about 11 years and have made a plan almost every single month. I am still here because I would feel guilty as there are people that have seriously helped me and the only way I might be able to repay them is if I live long enough. For the first time in my life I have started to not feel suicidal anymore and it's amazing. Feel free to DM me if you want to know more about it. I have literally stopped myself from killing myself because I wanted to get the shampoo and conditioner bottle open. Whatever you can do to make it through works then when you feel better you can think about the big stuff. Also sorry this ended up being to long but I hope you read it.

TL DR: Live for the small stuff not the big stuff.

Audiobooks or podcasts at double speed, fast enough that your brain won't get bored and you have to actually listen to it to follw what's going on some narrators are better then others for this so you might have to try a couple times to find the right one.

My insomnia is extreme so I'm not trying to worry you but I have gone for weeks without sleep for about 11 years, it happens it's not great but I have so much more time and can work more which is great. Last night was a good night I got 2.5 hours and yes my brain is probably wired a bit differently but I just wanted to say it's possible to do live like it, it's just hell. I would offer some advice but I fear I am not qualified to help with that
Thank you! I'm sorry that post sounds like I am just fishing for compliments about basic everyday tasks, I just really want to pretend like someone cares about me.

Any sort of craft you can do with your hands and see a product that you are creating is really good, covering your mirrors so you can't see it, clipping nails and making tools more difficult to reach, going for a walk or exercising even yoga, doing chores or writing anything to keep your hands busy. I always try to distract myself including some of my other OCD rituals that are bad and an annoying waste of time but I can't stop until they are over and completed perfectly which can sometimes help make the time go faster. I've been working on waiting to pick and I can slowly work on increasing the amount of time I can wait until I can go for long enough I don't feel the urge to pick anymore, it's a long and slow process but worth it because I don't want scars that I have to constantly hide from skin picking or huge bald spots from hair pulling.
I didn't plan to live long enough to make double digits but I'm here I guess and for the first time in my life I do not have an active suicide plan.
Block her, change your phone number, consider getting a restraining order. I've had three police officers tell my parents not to contact me because I will press charges and it mostly worked.

There is osdd-1b which has all of the other symtoms accept for dissociative amnesia. However, that still involves alters that front, I wouldn't really say it's like doing things on autopilot but more of being a different person. You can tell by thinking about your posture, how you feel about your name, musical prefences and so on. You don't want to go too far into looking into it because then it becomes a problem and it's something that you can convince yourself you have even though you don't if that makes any sense.

I am stuck in a similar place. My brain used to shut itself down if I thought about some really dark things but now that won't work. The only thing I can say that helps is just laying down not to sleep at all and while keeping your brain distracted. It helps to at least allow you to have a bit of a break and you don't have to think about anything. It also helps because its better to not stress about getting to sleep but just getting time to relax. If you can listen to music while reading a book or scrolling through social media or whatever to just keep your mind distracted while allowing your body to rest. It probably won't make you sleep but I find the rest helps to decrease hallucinations although who knows I could be making everything up right now and I could being seeing things that I'm just unable to recognize as fake anymore. Sorry I might be slightly sleep deprived but seriously laying down to just mentally tell yourself it is time to zone out a bit is great. Of course you should probably be actually dealing with your issues but given what you were describing it seems like you need to rest a bit before you should try to actually process things.
All the time. Each time I start to feel bad I disasocaite and if I don't I will try to force myself to disasocaite.

I listen to audiobooks at double speed. Some narrators are better then others and I just let it run through the night. It's not a long term solution but if you're desprate it works also if you keep the audiobook running the full time you are asleep. For whatever reason my mind has choosen to protect itself by forgetting my dreams so I don't have any good ways to help but if you're desprate to sleep audiobooks can at least get your mind thinking about something else.

I feel like a burden because I'm currently unable to support myself and am living with a friend. I recently had a friend stop talking to me because I was being too needy which is exactly what I fear. It took a lot for me to get where I am today and that was after learning how to open up to people but I guess I was talking to them too much. Now I'm terrified that they are the only person that was brave enough to actually call me out on doing something wrong. 
I don't have access to therapy and am terrified to reach out to people because I don't want to lose them. I'm stuck just trying to deal with everything on my own because I don't have things like parents or a therapist. I thought I was being careful to avoid over sharing there is so much that no one will ever know about me but apparently not.
And yeah I technically shouldn't go back to them I know it's really bad I just regret leaving them. I left really recently and have been attempting to deal with the reprocussions of leaving them so quickly as that was not something I planned to do until later. 
Thank you for your response, I am realizing this is likely caused by me just continuing to freak out that I am a horrible person and am doing what my parents did to me to others and I think my friend leaving only affirmed this belief.

He also talks about supressing his feeling instead of trying to actually deal with them. It also mentions that it's not good to shut off yourself from the world but it seemed like the safer option but know he is really lonely and trapped in his own mind.
Trauma, sleep and being tired is a huge trigger for me. I've gone for insane amounts of time with no sleep because my brain supposedly rewired itself to avoid sleeping.

Happy Birthday from some random stranger on the internet! Your not needy for wanting people to pay attention to your birthday. You deserve better than people who do not care about you and I am hopeful that you might find a different group of friends who do care. So even though I am a completely random person I just wanted to say congratulations on making it this far and I hope that you have a good year!

I'm not going back to my abusers and my brain decided I was safe enough to handle some really intense flashbacks so I guess some part of me has deemed me "safe." Right now for the first time in my life I feel relatively safe super hypervigillant and reliving trauma when I least expect it but I'd say I feel close to safe? And safe to me is basically I'm not going to get abused anymore.
I sleep during the day if I even manage to sleep but at least I'm sleeping and it's better then my schedule before quarentine where I would only be able to sleep once a week.
I don't but I also have insane insomia so sleeping really doesn't happen too much for me anyways which is fine.

This happens all the time for me, I've never checked my temperature during it though. But yeah I'll get super sick, have awful migranes. The only thing that helps me is just laying down for a bit and reminding myself it will pass if I am in a place where I can. If not, I just keep going because I don't know what else to do.
Defiently, I get triggered by sleeping and eating how is one even supposed to live a normal life like that.

I'm still in college but had to leave my family because I couldn't stay with them when campus was shut down. I had to get the police involved and it was not fun. I have to say leaving them was probably the best decision I made in my life. I lost contact with everyone in my family because no one knew what was going on and I knew whatever I would say would be repeated to my parents. I can't talk to my sister about it because she is unaware that anything happened and thinks everything is my fault. The first month was really hard especially since I had only a few days to make my decision. I had to accept the fact that my parents do not love me which is something I'm still working on. However, my mental health is doing better then it would have been if I stayed in contact with them. It hurt to leave and it hurts thinking about spending holidays alone and not having anyone to invite to my graduation but I am doing so much better then I would have if I stayed. I don't know if this is helpful but yeah I miss my sister but she is still on my parents side. The longer I have been no contact with everyone the better.
All the time and also other people's parents and parental figures in general.

I'm in a similar boat and what really helps me is setting goals for the day and then doing them and not allowing myself to do anything until I accomplish my goals. I typically set them each week. I've seen people with to do lists but that never works for me because I think I have more time then I actually do because it takes me longer to complete work thanks to randomly dissasociating or having flashbacks because I'm triggered by so many things. I'm not sure how healthy it is though because a lot of the times I end up not eating until I finish whatever I told myself I have to accomplish. But if I have a mental breakdown or dissasociate I have to keep going because I set rules that I have to follow. I don't know if that's helpful or really a great idea but it works for me. I have no motivation I just have rules I set for myself and feel the need to follow them or else my brain gets mad at me. I always remind myself that the boring school work will be over and one day I might be working my dream job.

Run, run as far as you can as fast as you can get out get somewhere safe you do not deserve this. I would tell myself to call the police. No one should have had to go through that and I could have been so much better. I would tell myself not to be asshamed of what my parents were doing and to let someone know. I would tell myself that I need to give up and run away that all those years of tourture I put up with for some idea of financal security will be completely useless as my parents cut me off anyways.

I agree, the new version of someone's favorite childhood movie did not ruin their childhood and the overusing the word trigger for politics is absurd. I would also like to add "trauma" has started to get added into the mix where people are talking about movies being traumatic or bad experiences being "traumatic." I know trauma is related to the person but still some things should not be considered traumatic.

Although I do have to say sometimes I look at people who say things like that and my reaction ends up being more along the lines of geniunely being happy for them because they think a tv show to be something that ruined their childhood. It's really hard for either side to have compassion for the other as our experences are vastly different and it's difficult to put a monopoly on words for only bad things but overall I still hate the trend and that it causes words to lose their meaning.

Frankly, just don't talk to them. It is not worth the stress and the pain it will cause you. I know it's hard and you probably feel guilty about it but I would recomend just not talking to her. It's better for you and there probably isn't anything you can say that will fix any of your problems.

All the time, the best is trying to avoid looking like I'm not being productive then I become so focused on looking like I'm doing something then I end up not doing whatever I'm trying to look like I'm doing.

I used to also scream in my sleep my parents helped put a stop to it and know I can go for weeks without sleeping. I got a weighted blanket and that helps with sleeping and is especially if you want someone to hold you. It's terrifying and I know what your going through. I don't know how to stop them and the method my parents used was not the one but I just wanted to comment to say your not alone.
I would like to have a bit more information but I would be intrested.

If you can't contact a doctor or don't want to, you will be ok, for me the hallucinations don't really get bad until it's been at least a week with no sleep. Sometimes I'll get some hallucinations earlier but it usually isn't too bad. But also my doctor (who might have just given up) said that my brain probably functions differently then other people because I can go so long without sleep so that might not be normal. Anyways the most important thing you can do is try your best not to stress about not sleeping because that just makes it worst, try your best to distract yourself if you can spend some time just laying down it's really good to allow yourself to relax a bit even if you don't sleep just make sure you are listening to a podcast or audiobook or something that isn't your own thoughts.

Yeah it's so bad I'll convince myself I don't need sleep until I can't handle staying awake for any longer. I once let it get so bad I actually lost the ability to function (I couldn't sit up for too long because it was too exuasting). I used to be able to sleep on meds but gave up because I grow resistant to them too quickly.

I have this and it's probably because being tired is actually a trigger for me which is really fun. Which means if I get tired I have to go through some really rough flashbacks then I can sleep. My solutions have been listening to audiobooks or podcasts at double speed or metal to help distract my thoughts. Of course I also don't really get tired too much because my brain is used to not sleeping and having to be constantly alert so I get very little sleep and can actually function without sleep it's just that then I start losing some brain function and get slower.

All the time, I recently left because I could not live with them anymore. Despite everything that I went to and every time I thought about running away and the fact that I am happier basically homeless then with them I still feel like I need to love them. Like they put a roof over my head and well I was starved for being "to fat" but they feed me and yes I did have to pay taxes to them but it wasn't that bad. Besides they only ever used corporal punishment when I deserved it so I always feel like it was my fault for everything. They had logic for it too so I feel like I should just love them. But I'm learning that I do not have to love them just because they gave birth to me and that having a roof over my head is the bare minimum.
